text: Breathing and kicking are essential components of swimming. A swimming stroke typically lasts 10-15 seconds. The first stage involves the downward flow of air into the lungs, releasing air and water simultaneously. The water is drawn in through the lungs, into the upper chest cavity and the lower chest cavity. The second stage involves lifting the feet and performing the stroke, which lasts around 10-15 seconds. The third stage involves lifting the head and performing the stroke, lasting approximately 2-3 seconds. The final stage involves lifting the torso and performing the stroke, lasting around 2-3 seconds. The arms and stroke also take around 2-3 seconds to complete.
